informal_statement: For homeomorphic topological spaces `M` and `N` related by a homeomorphism `e`, applying the inverse homeomorphism `e.symm` to a point `x` in `N` retrieves the corresponding point `y` in `M` such that `e(y)` maps back to `x`.
informal_proof: Given a homeomorphism `e: M ≃ₜ N`, the inverse function `e.symm` provides the necessary correspondence in reverse. By the properties of homeomorphisms—specifically, the bijectivity and continuity of `e` and its inverse—applying `e.symm` to `x` yields exactly the point `y` in `M` that was paired with `x` via `e`. This ensures that `e.symm x = y` if and only if `x = e y`, which is formally stated by the lemma `Equiv.symm_apply_eq`.

/-- A subset of a topological space is homeomorphic to its image under a homeomorphism.

@[simps!]
def image (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (s : Set X) : s ≃ₜ e '' s where
  -- Porting note (https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/issues/11215): TODO: by continuity!
  continuous_toFun := e.continuous.continuousOn.restrict_mapsTo (mapsTo_image _ _)
  continuous_invFun := (e.symm.continuous.comp continuous_subtype_val).codRestrict _
  toEquiv := e.toEquiv.image s

rag.name: Homeomorph
rag.content:
/-- Homeomorphism between `X` and `Y`, also called topological isomorphism -/
structure Homeomorph (X : Type*) (Y : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
    extends X ≃ Y where
  /-- The forward map of a homeomorphism is a continuous function. -/
  continuous_toFun : Continuous toFun := by continuity
  /-- The inverse map of a homeomorphism is a continuous function. -/
  continuous_invFun : Continuous invFun := by continuity

informal_statement: If two topological spaces A and B are homeomorphic via a homeomorphism e, then the topology on B is exactly the topology induced by pulling back the open sets from A using e.
informal_proof:
We are given a homeomorphism \( e: A \rightarrow B \) between two topological spaces \( A \) and \( B \). By definition, a homeomorphism is a continuous bijection with a continuous inverse. 

The topology \( \tau_B \) on \( B \) being equal to the coinduced topology \( \tau_A.coinduced e \) means that each open set in \( B \) is precisely the image of an open set in \( A \) under \( e \). This follows because, for any open set \( U \subseteq A \), the set \( e[U] \subseteq B \) is open by the definition of the coinduced topology. Conversely, since \( e \) is a homeomorphism, every open set \( V \subseteq B \) must be the image under \( e \) of an open set in \( A \), specifically \( e^{-1}[V] \) is open in \( A \), hence \( V = e[e^{-1}[V]] \) is open in \( B \).

Thus, under the homeomorphism \( e \), the topology on \( B \) is precisely the one induced by \( \tau_A \), ensuring that \( e \) preserves all topological structures.
